title: The missing roof changes what you see
position: Central nave and adjacent clerestory remains.
question: Why make the middle columns taller?
observation: The height difference leaves space for stone-grilled windows.
explanation: Roof slabs rested on architraves; the clerestory admitted light above the lower side roofs. The present open sky is not the ancient lighting arrangement.
lookFor: Trace the load path: capital, abacus, architrave, former roof slabs.
Identify the window level rather than assuming the gaps are ordinary doorways.

claims.text: Columns supported architraves and roof slabs.
The raised nave created room for grilled clerestory windows; the roofed hall admitted much less light than today.

uncertainties: No numerical reconstruction of ancient light levels is available here.
Do not infer exact intended symbolism from engineering alone.
